bug_description.original: A vulnerability in kex.c within the ecdh_sha2_nistp() function allows the function to attempt to parse malformed data due to improper handling of input buffers.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 550-byte witness is written verbatim to libssh2's socketpair-based OSS-Fuzz harness and reaches ECDH key exchange. `kex_method_ecdh_key_exchange()` retrieves an `SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY` packet and passes its heap-backed payload to `ecdh_sha2_nistp()`. That function only checks `data_len < 5`, then skips the packet-type byte, reads the next four bytes as `session->server_hostkey_len`, and the saved AddressSanitizer run shows this length becomes 25089. The vulnerable code allocates a destination buffer of that size and immediately `memcpy()`s `session->server_hostkey_len` bytes from the reply buffer without validating that the length-prefixed host-key field fits inside the received packet. AddressSanitizer reports that the source buffer is only a 24-byte heap allocation from `_libssh2_transport_read()`, so the copy overruns the end of the reply buffer and crashes at `src/kex.c:1773`. The fix replaces this raw pointer parsing with `struct string_buf` plus `_libssh2_copy_string()` / `_libssh2_get_string()`, which check each length-prefixed field against the remaining packet bounds before copying.

source.description: The ECDH reply parser skips the packet-type byte and decodes the next four attacker-controlled bytes as `session->server_hostkey_len`, materializing the copy size later used by `memcpy()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 550-byte socket stream sent directly to `libssh2_session_handshake()`. On the saved crashing path, `kex_method_ecdh_key_exchange()` receives an `SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY` buffer backed by the 24-byte heap allocation reported by ASan, and bytes 1..4 of that reply payload decode here to the eventual 25089-byte copy length.

sink.description: ASan sink. The copy reads `session->server_hostkey_len` bytes from `s == data + 5`; the saved crash shows the reply buffer is only a 24-byte heap allocation, so this read crosses the end of that buffer.

root_cause.description: After decoding the untrusted host-key length, the vulnerable code allocates a destination buffer of that size and proceeds toward the copy without any check that the length-prefixed field actually fits in the received reply buffer. The staged patch replaces this manual sequence with `_libssh2_copy_string()` on a bounded `struct string_buf`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This 32-bit length field becomes the host-key copy size. On the saved crashing run it evaluates to 25089, matching the ASan-reported read size at the sink.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crashing stack contains `kex_method_ecdh_key_exchange -> ecdh_sha2_nistp`, so the fuzzed socket stream is accepted far enough for libssh2 to request and obtain an `SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY` packet before the crash.

coarse_trace.summary: The handshake waits for an `SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY` packet and passes the matched reply buffer into `ecdh_sha2_nistp()`.
The ECDH reply parser only enforces `data_len >= 5`, then manually treats the host key as a length-prefixed field and decodes an attacker-controlled `server_hostkey_len` from the packet.
It allocates a destination buffer sized by that untrusted length and `memcpy()`s 25089 bytes from the small reply buffer, producing the ASan-reported heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: `_libssh2_packet_require()` retrieves the reply packet that `ecdh_sha2_nistp()` will parse and stores its buffer pointer and logical length in `key_state`. The saved ASan allocation stack shows the backing heap allocation for that reply buffer comes from `_libssh2_transport_read()` and is 24 bytes long.

The only upfront bound check requires enough bytes for the packet type plus one 32-bit length field. The witness passes this minimum guard, so later code may trust a nested host-key length even though no check yet proves that the full length-prefixed field fits in the reply buffer.

Manual parsing advances to `data + 1` and interprets the next four reply bytes as `session->server_hostkey_len`. On the saved run this becomes 25089, matching ASan's reported read size; after `s += 4`, the subsequent copy source begins at `data + 5`.

The destination extent is now exactly the untrusted length 25089. No check enforces that the reply buffer still contains that many bytes after `data + 5`; the patch replaces this raw allocation-and-copy sequence with `_libssh2_copy_string()` on a `struct string_buf`, which validates the remaining length before copying.

ASan sink. `memcpy()` reads 25089 bytes from `s == data + 5`. The saved crash proves the source buffer is only a 24-byte heap allocation, so at most 19 bytes are addressable from `data + 5` before the copy reads off the end of the reply buffer.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the over-read source buffer was allocated here as a 24-byte heap region before `_libssh2_packet_require()` handed it to the ECDH reply parser.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch stops manually walking raw pointer `s` through the ECDH reply and instead parses the host key, server public key, and signature through `_libssh2_copy_string()` / `_libssh2_get_string()` on a bounded `struct string_buf`. Those helpers call `_libssh2_check_length()` before copying, so the malformed length-prefixed host-key field is rejected before the crashing `memcpy()`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this is a source-level conclusion from the staged diff rather than fixed-runtime evidence.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan's allocation stack identifies the small reply buffer that later serves as the `memcpy()` source, and the traced root cause is the unchecked nested length field that makes the copy read beyond that same buffer.

poc.trigger: The staged 550-byte file `poc` is sent verbatim to the socketpair by `ssh2_client_fuzzer`. Stage 01's saved run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 25089` in `ecdh_sha2_nistp` at `src/kex.c:1773`.

format.name: libssh2 ssh2_client_fuzzer raw socket stream
format.contract: Raw byte stream consumed as the server side of `libssh2_session_handshake()`. To preserve the witnessed path, the stream must reach `kex_method_ecdh_key_exchange()` and supply an `SSH2_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY` packet whose host-key length field, the four bytes immediately after the reply packet-type byte, decodes to the witnessed value 25089 even though the reply buffer later over-read by `memcpy()` is only a 24-byte heap allocation.
